title: Evaluation protocol, not model architecture, drives reported accuracy in fNIRS spatial-attention decoding: analysis code
description: Analysis code for a secondary analysis of the public fNIRS dataset OpenNeuro ds004830 (three-class spatial attention under competing talkers, 12 participants). Holding data, features and classifiers fixed, the code evaluates four cross-validation protocols drawn from the published fNIRS literature and shows that the choice of train/test split alone moves three-class accuracy by 46.6 percentage points, from 32.72 percent under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation to 79.28 percent when channels are treated as independent samples. Also included is a reconstruction of the trial onsets, which are absent from the released BIDS events files, validated against a shuffled-onset control, a global lag sweep, and the original authors' published behavioural accuracies. The dataset itself is not redistributed here.
